The UK's 20 Greatest Motorcycle Roads

Britain may be small, but its road network is extraordinarily diverse. We've ridden thousands of miles across every corner of the UK to compile this definitive list. These are the roads that make you glad you ride — the ones you'll remember long after you've parked up and taken off your helmet.

1. Bealach na Bà, Highland Scotland

Britain's greatest road. Period. The Bealach na Bà rises 626m in just a few miles, with Alpine-style hairpins, cattle grids, and views that stretch to the Outer Hebrides. It's steep, it's narrow, and it's utterly magnificent. Ride it anti-clockwise from Applecross for the most dramatic ascent.

2. A82 Glen Coe, Highland Scotland

The A82 through Glen Coe is motorcycling's answer to a cathedral — vast, humbling, and unforgettable. The road flows beautifully through the glacial valley with the Buachaille Etive Mor standing sentinel at its eastern entrance.

3. Black Mountain Road (A4069), Wales

Wales' finest — a swooping, open road across the Black Mountain with tight hairpins and panoramic views. The tarmac is smooth and the bends are perfectly shaped for a flowing ride.

4-10: The Upper Echelon

  • 4. A686 Hartside Pass — England's great climb, 580m of pure riding pleasure
  • 5. A87 Glen Shiel — Scotland's most scenic A-road, mountains on both sides
  • 6. Hardknott Pass — England's steepest and most challenging road, 30% gradients
  • 7. Cat and Fiddle (A537) — The Pennines' best-known biking road, sweeping moorland bends
  • 8. Snake Pass (A57) — Classic Pennine road through wild moorland
  • 9. A543 Denbigh Moors — Wales' secret weapon, fast and flowing across open heath
  • 10. B3212 Dartmoor — Wild ponies, granite tors, and open Devon moorland

11-20: The Best of the Rest

  • 11. A838 Durness to Lairg — Remote Highland touring at its finest
  • 12. Military Road, Northumberland — Hadrian's Wall country, empty and atmospheric
  • 13. Llanberis Pass (A4086) — Snowdonia at its most dramatic
  • 14. A39 Atlantic Highway — Devon and Cornwall coastal drama
  • 15. A93 Cairngorm Pass — Britain's highest main road
  • 16. Gospel Pass, Wales — Hidden gem above Hay-on-Wye
  • 17. B4391 Bala to Ffestiniog — Welsh mountain riding perfected
  • 18. A595/A5092 Cumbrian Coast — Underrated coastal and fell scenery
  • 19. A702 Devil's Beeftub — Scottish Borders classic with a dark history
  • 20. B3306 St Ives to Land's End — Cornwall's wildest coastal road
Every one of these roads has been ridden, rated, and road-tested by the VisorUp team. These aren't internet lists — they're battle-tested recommendations.

How We Rated Them

Our ranking considered five factors: scenery, road surface quality, bend variety, traffic levels, and overall riding experience. Scotland dominates because its roads combine stunning scenery with minimal traffic. Wales offers incredible value — concentrated brilliance in a compact country. keyTakeaways: The Bealach na Ba tops the list, rising 626 metres in a few miles with Alpine-style hairpins and cattle grids.
Scotland dominates the rankings thanks to stunning scenery combined with minimal traffic.
Wales offers concentrated brilliance, with the A4069 Black Mountain Road ranked third overall.
England's hard-won entries include the A686 Hartside Pass and the 30% gradients of Hardknott Pass.
Roads were rated on scenery, surface quality, bend variety, traffic levels and overall riding experience.

faq.q: Which is the UK's greatest motorcycle road?
faq.a: The Bealach na Ba in Highland Scotland takes top spot. It rises 626 metres in just a few miles with Alpine-style hairpins, cattle grids and views to the Outer Hebrides. Ride it anti-clockwise from Applecross for the most dramatic ascent up the pass.

The ranking considered five factors: scenery, road surface quality, bend variety, traffic levels and overall riding experience. Scotland dominates because its roads combine stunning scenery with minimal traffic, while Wales offers concentrated brilliance in a compact country and England's entries are harder-won but rewarding.

faq.q: Why does Scotland feature so heavily?
faq.a: Scotland's roads pair world-class scenery with some of the lowest traffic levels in Britain, which scores highly across every rating factor. Roads such as the A82 through Glen Coe and the A87 through Glen Shiel deliver cathedral-scale landscapes with flowing tarmac, so they naturally rise to the top of the list.

faq.q: Can I ride these roads in a single trip?
faq.a: Not comfortably, as they span from Cornwall to the far Scottish north. Most riders tackle them by region: a Highlands trip for the Scottish entries, a Snowdonia and Brecon loop for Wales, and Lake District or Peak District weekends for the English classics. Plan clusters rather than one continuous marathon.
